question:
In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, take the electrostatic potential energy of an electron–proton system to be zero at infinite separation, i.e., $U(\infty)=0$.

Assume the electron (mass $m_e$, charge magnitude $e$) moves in a circular orbit of radius $r$ with speed $v$ around the proton, held by Coulomb attraction. Use the given relations:

1) Centripetal condition: $\dfrac{m_ev^2}{r}=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r^2}$.

2) Potential energy: $U(r)=-\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r}$.

Evaluate why the total mechanical energy $E=K+U$ of a bound electron in hydrogen must be negative.

(i) Derive the relation between kinetic energy $K$ and potential energy $U$ for a Bohr orbit (core derivation).

(ii) Hence obtain the sign of $E$ and interpret it physically using the reference state at infinity (application/inference).

(iii) If an electron in a bound orbit has total energy $E=-5.0\,\text{eV}$, evaluate the minimum energy required to make it a free electron at rest at infinity, and justify your conclusion.

options.A: Using $U(\infty)=0$ and the derived relation $K=-\dfrac{U}{2}$, the total energy is $E=K+U=\dfrac{U}{2}<0$ for any finite $r$; therefore energy must be supplied equal to $|E|$ (here $5.0\,\text{eV}$) to free the electron to rest at infinity.
options.B: Kinetic energy can be negative in quantum systems, so $E<0$ without any further relation between $K$ and $U$; the minimum energy needed is $0\,\text{eV}$.
options.C: Because the proton repels the electron, $U>0$ and hence $E<0$ automatically; the minimum energy needed is $5.0\,\text{eV}$.
options.D: In stable orbits, $K=0$ and only $U<0$ exists, so $E=U<0$; the minimum energy needed is $2.5\,\text{eV}$.
